checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate but slightly lenient on the 'Legs' checkpoint. While the standing dog's legs are correct, the lying dog's paws (part of the 'narrow feet' description) show structural ambiguity (mushiness/fusion) which the Router noted as an artifact but still marked the checkpoint as 'present'. I agree with marking it present for the primary subject, but the secondary subject's defect should weigh on the alignment score. The 'Gait' checkpoint was correctly identified as untestable.
artifact_review: The Router identified fusion at the intersection and texture anomalies in the paws. The severity ratings (2.5 and 1.5) are appropriate. The topology auditor's mask confidence is high, but this only confirms a coherent blob, not internal anatomical correctness. The pose auditor's low-confidence keypoints on the lying dog (hips/knees) corroborate the visual 'mushiness' of the tucked limbs. No new catastrophic artifacts were found, but the limb definition issues are notable.
alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the Borzoi class. The fine-grained classifier confirmed the breed with high confidence (logit 7.18). Key morphological features (long snout, roached back, ear set) are present and correct on the standing dog. The lying dog also conforms to the general shape, though specific limb details are less distinct. 8/8 testable checkpoints passed visually.
artifact_reasoning: Structural integrity is good overall, but there are minor defects typical of multi-subject AI generation. Fusion occurs where the dogs overlap, making boundary separation difficult. The paws of the lying dog lack distinct digit definition (texture anomaly/structural softness), supported by low-confidence pose keypoints in the hind/front limb regions. These are moderate issues that prevent a perfect score but do not constitute failure.
key_defects: Fusion/blur at the intersection of the two dogs
Ill-defined/mushy paws on the lying dog
Low pose confidence in tucked limbs of the lying dog
